title: PS-7 Vitamin and mineral supplementation to gestating F0 beef heifers and the multigenerational impacts on organ weights and circulating hormones and metabolites in the F1 Dam and F2 Fetus
content:
Abstract
This study assessed the impacts of providing a vitamin and mineral supplement to F0 beef heifers during gestation on organ weights, and hormone and metabolite concentrations in F1 offspring and F2 fetuses during pregnancy. Angus-crossbred heifers (F0; n = 72; 14 to 15 mo. of age, initial body weight [BW] 380.4 ± 50.56 kg) were ranked by BW, bred via artificial insemination (AI) using female-sexed semen, and randomly assigned at breeding to receive either: 1) a basal diet (n = 36 CON) or 2) a basal diet plus a vitamin and mineral supplement (n = 36 VTM). Pregnant F0 heifers were managed on their respective treatments until calving and then all F0/F1 cow-calf pairs were managed on a common diet until weaning. The F1 heifers (n = 14 CON; n = 17 VTM) were bred at 14 to 15 months of age via AI using female-sexed semen and were fed a common diet. Blood samples were collected from F1 dams on d 89.3 ± 0.58, 179.3 ± 0.68, and 250.4 ± 0.83 of gestation (slaughter) to represent the end of each trimester of pregnancy, and from F2 fetuses (n = 7 CON; n = 8 VTM) at slaughter. At slaughter, maternal and fetal tissues were collected and weighed. Blood serum samples were analyzed for concentrations of glucose, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), non-esterified fatty acids (NEFA), insulin, and insulin like growth factor-1 (IGF-1). Individual animals were the experimental unit and analyses were performed using the MIXED procedure of SAS for the main effect of treatment, day, and their interaction. Significance was considered at P ≤ 0.05 and tendencies declared at P > 0.05 and P ≤ 0.10. The F1 heifers from dams receiving VTM were heavier throughout gestation (P = 0.001) than CON, and hot carcass BW and ribeye area of the F1 VTM dams at slaughter tended (P ≤ 0.10) to be greater than the CON cohort. However, the F1 CON dams tended (P = 0.04) to have greater spleen weights as a percentage of BW compared with VTM. The spleen and reproductive tract weights also tended (P ≤ 0.10) to be heavier in CON than VTM F2 fetuses as a percentage of BW. The F1 heifers from dams receiving VTM had increased (P ≤ 0.01) concentrations of insulin and IGF-1 throughout pregnancy, and their F2 fetuses had greater concentrations of glucose (P = 0.01) compared with CON. These results indicate that the F1 BW and carcass traits are impacted by F0 treatment; however, organ weights across multiple generations of offspring were minimally affected. Nevertheless, hormone and metabolite concentrations were impacted transgenerationally, which may have relevance for improving efficiency of beef cattle production through maternal nutritional management strategies.
